chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ismail ibn Yasar, from Amr ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When forty men are present with the deceased and they say, 'O Allah, we do not know from him except good,' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I have accepted your testimony and forgiven him for what I know of what you do not know.'

key_terms.مِمَّا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ: From what you do not know

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of forty men testifying for the deceased in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores the efficacy of communal testimony (shahada) in granting divine mercy, specifically illustrating how forty men's declaration of the deceased's goodness triggers Allah's acceptance of their limited knowledge as sufficient for forgiveness of unknown sins. This reflects the scholarly view that the collective witness of the righteous can intercede for the dead, bridging the gap between human perception and divine omniscience. The narrative emphasizes the spiritual weight of gathering for the deceased, reinforcing the importance of communal prayer and remembrance in Shia funerary practices.
